This occurred because oil price increases demanded more dollars from importers, causing them to sell Treasuries, while Gulf producers could not recycle dollars due to the Strait closure. Thus the petrodollar mechanism broke.
arguments.conclusion_supported: The Iran war has shattered the normal safe-haven demand for Treasuries, revealing the petrodollar system's failure to maintain dollar dominance during this crisis.
